title: I'm making Brutal Soccer: arcade football with no referee, tackles and a super shot that can knock out the players
author: alpargataman
selftext:
Hi! I've been making Brutal Soccer, an arcade football game that runs in the browser. There's no referee, so nothing is a foul.

What's in it right now:

* A slide tackle takes o a hit with the ball takes some of the HP every player has. Hit 0 and you're out for 10 seconds, seeing stars, then you're back with 30 HP.
* Fill your team's SUPER bar and fire the Tornado: an S-curve shot that goes straight through defenders. Only the keeper can stop it, and only with HP to spare.
* Multiple stadiums with objects, obstacles and environmental modifications.
* Up to 4 players on one screen, with gamepads or a keyboard: all on one team against the AI, or split between both teams.
* Online, up to 8 players (4 per team). Matches are always 7-a-side, and the AI fills the empty spots.
* It's free and it plays in the browser, on desktop or on a phone in landscape (the touch controls are a first version).
* The UI is in Spanish for now. English is next.

The trailer is in-engine footage. The shots tagged "In-engine camera" use camera angles that aren't in the game.

After a lot of time and many tests with many models, I think the game is reaching a playable status and I'm looking for some opinions about the feeling or the idea.

Thanks in advice.

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/alpargataman this post needs more detail on how you used AI in development. Saying you used AI isn't the same as explaining how. Rule 4 asks promotional posts to contribute by talking about the process. We're trying to keep "check out my game" posts from taking over the sub. If you don't update, this may be removed.

replies.author: alpargataman
replies.body:
To develop the game, I used AI from almost the beginning of the development. I'm vibecoding everything with JavaScript and three.js. I started the development of the game before summer and switched models from opus 4.5 to GPT 5, to Fable 5, to GPT6, to Opus 5.5. Now, I'm working a lot with Opus 5.5 using images from other games for the design, asking for tests and making iterations.

First, I planned everything and created a private repo on GitHub where I have the issues with all the things I want to work on the game. After, that, I ask Opus to verify those issues and start working on them. Finally, I play some matches and ask Opus for some tests and adjustments.

For me, it's the first time I've reached this status trying to develop a game, and I always wanted to make a football (soccer) game without rules inspired on Nintendo World Cup and Mario Strikers and thanks to the AI I'm doing that.
